guide.summary: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none); Public app serving multiple Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new app submissions, longer reported).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app serving multiple Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new app submissions, longer reported).

composio.note: Composio lists Zendesk as managed OAuth, but the docs do not say which Zendesk auth methods are managed. Check the toolkit's composio_managed_auth_schemes field.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed app. For production you likely need your own: Zendesk requires a global OAuth client for multi-customer apps, and a managed app shows Composio branding and shares quota.
reasons: Show your own brand on the consent screen
Restrict scopes to what you need
Get dedicated rate-limit quota instead of shared quota
Zendesk requires a global OAuth client for apps distributed to multiple customers

scenarios.label: Internal use, your own Zendesk account
scenarios.when_this_applies: The agent only acts on your company's own Zendesk account, not on customers' accounts.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No provider review described for this setup

scenarios.approval: No review found for local OAuth clients; the global client requirement does not apply to internal use.

scenarios.label: Public app serving multiple Zendesk customers
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent product connects many customers' Zendesk accounts, which is the usual production setup.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.estimate: 1-3 weeks for new app submissions, longer reported
waiting.basis: c17 stated turnaround; c18 and c19 report recent delays. No time found for the global client request itself.

scenarios.approval: Zendesk must approve a global OAuth client request. Marketplace publishing is reviewed separately.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk admin account
prerequisites.detail: Creating an OAuth client requires a Zendesk admin.

prerequisites.title: Sponsored developer account (d3v-)
prerequisites.detail: The global client request must come from a d3v- account; others are not accepted.

prerequisites.title: Developer portal organization
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization on the Marketplace developer portal before submitting.

steps.title: Create local OAuth client
steps.detail: Sign in as a Zendesk admin and create a Confidential client. Save the identifier and secret.
steps.done_when: You hold the client identifier and secret.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and register it exactly on the client.
steps.done_when: Redirect URL on the client matches Composio's value.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Prepare global client request
steps.detail: Draft scope list from the endpoints you call. Check the client uses a zdg- identifier with all fields filled.

steps.title: Submit global OAuth request
steps.detail: In the Marketplace portal, choose Global OAuth, then Request new OAuth. Note the secret and identifier first, since you lose access to the client page after conversion.
steps.done_when: You receive an email and a ticket reference.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk approval
steps.detail: Zendesk's Marketplace Operations team approves and converts the client.
steps.done_when: Zendesk converts your client to global.

steps.title: Handle token refresh
steps.detail: Ensure authorization requests pass expires_in for older clients and refresh tokens are stored on each refresh.

traps.title: Token expiry is being enforced
traps.detail: Access tokens default to 30 minutes and refresh tokens to 30 days. Enforcement on existing local clients rolls out in waves from June 30, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

traps.title: Refresh tokens rotate
traps.detail: Each refresh deletes the previous access and refresh tokens, so store the new pair. Existing tokens cannot be refreshed.

traps.title: Review delays beyond the stated time
traps.detail: A developer reported an update stuck for nearly three weeks, and Zendesk acknowledged response times past its normal SLAs.

traps.title: Client identifier cannot change later
traps.detail: The identifier must start with zdg-, be the exact production value, and be representative of your product.

traps.title: Scopes locked after approval
traps.detail: Zendesk may restrict the client to allowed scopes. Requests outside them fail with invalid_scope, and changes require contacting Zendesk Support.

traps.title: Product coverage is limited
traps.detail: The global client process applies only to Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled).

traps.title: Managed app limits
traps.detail: Managed apps show Composio branding and share quota across all Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Using a regular OAuth or API token for multiple customers
blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk prohibits customers sharing credentials with you, so multi-customer apps need global OAuth tokens.
blockers.what_to_do: Request a global OAuth client from Zendesk.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request details and check the local client fields.

blockers.what_it_means: The app requested a scope outside the client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or ask Zendesk Support to update them.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the allowed list.

open_questions: How long does the global OAuth client request take? Not found; ask Zendesk Support or check the ticket updates after submitting.
Is a Marketplace listing required for the global client, or only for being listed? Docs unclear; ask Zendesk Marketplace support.
Which Zendesk auth methods does Composio manage? Check composio_managed_auth_schemes in the Zendesk toolkit.
Does Zendesk verify redirect-URI domains? Only an exact-match rule was found.

claims.text: A global OAuth client is required when distributing a public or integration app to multiple Zendesk customers.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If you distribute a public app or an integration app to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate requests.

claims.text: The global-client requirement does not apply to apps built for internal use.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: This requirement doesn't apply if you're developing applications or integrations for internal use.

claims.text: Developers cannot create their own global OAuth clients; they must request one from Zendesk.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: For security reasons, Zendesk doesn't allow developers to create their own global OAuth clients.

claims.text: Zendesk converts the local OAuth client into a global one only if the request is approved.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The global client request is submitted once the app is finished and ready to be used across multiple Zendesk accounts.

claims.quote: When your app is finished and ready to use across multiple Zendesk accounts, submit your request as described below.

claims.text: The request subdomain must include the d3v- prefix; submissions from accounts without it are not accepted.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: A sponsored developer account can be requested for development, with instructions on a separate page.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: To request a sponsored developer account, see Getting a trial or sponsored account for development .

claims.text: All fields on the local client must be completed, even fields labeled optional.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Make sure all fields are completed for the local client. Even if a field is labeled optional, it is required for global clients.

claims.text: The client identifier must start with the string zdg-.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Ensure your Unique Identifier is prefixed with the string "zdg-".

claims.text: The client identifier should be the exact value intended for production.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: The client identifier should be the exact value intended for production.

claims.text: The client identifier must be representative of the product or business; a generic name like zdg-global_client1 is not acceptable.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: For example, "zdg-zendesk is acceptable" but "zdg-global_client1" is not.

claims.text: The client identifier and secret must be noted down before the request, because access to the client admin page is lost after conversion.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Make sure you note down the secret and the identifier before making your request.

claims.text: The developer should request only the scopes the app genuinely needs.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Provide only the scopes your app genuinely needs.

claims.text: Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on an approved global client to restrict it to the scopes the app needs.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: When Zendesk approves your global OAuth client, Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on the client to restrict it to the scopes your app needs.

claims.text: A request for a scope outside the allowed scopes fails with a 400 error and an invalid_scope error, and no token is issued.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If your app requests a scope that is not included in the client's allowed scopes, the authorization request fails with a 400 Bad Request response and an invalid_scope error — no token is issued.

claims.text: Changes to scope needs after approval require contacting Zendesk Support to update the allowed scopes.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If your app's scope requirements change after your global client has been approved, contact Zendesk Support to request an update to the client's allowed scopes.

claims.text: Zendesk's stated turnaround is 1-3 weeks for new app submissions and 1-2 weeks for updates to existing apps.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You can expect a turnaround time of 1-3 weeks for new app submissions and 1-2 week for updates to existing apps.

claims.text: A developer reported an app update stuck in validation for almost three weeks, which they linked to Zendesk's new OAuth/API security requirements.
claims.label: reported

claims.text: Zendesk's own reply acknowledged that a surge of submissions tied to its API security and OAuth guideline changes pushed review response times past normal SLAs.
claims.label: reported

claims.text: The global OAuth client instructions apply only to Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled) accounts.
